snippet.title: How to spot populist messaging.
snippet.description: How can you tell the difference between populist messaging and who’s actually fighting for the rest of us?  A lot of it has to do with follow through, but also WHO are politicians fighting for.  Everyone, or just the people who agree with them.  Everyone deserves access to affordable healthcare, and it’s worth paying attention to who is actually fighting for these issues.

----

Bet on anything markets have just had their best year ever. 
These platforms let you gamble (or sorry I mean TRADE), on everything from elections, to the number of starving children in active warzones all the way down to Jake Paul getting the snot beat out of him.
Now (as a shock to absolutely nobody) the proliferation of these markets is already having some… questionable… impacts on the state of our society, but that’s easy to ignore when these platforms are bringing in this much money. 
Just Kalshi and Polymarket (the two largest prediction markets right now) are on track to handle over a hundred billion dollars in trading volume this year alone, and other businesses have noticed this. 
The mass adoption of betting on everything has become so widespread that it’s threatening the thinly veiled gambling facilitated by platforms like robinhood and coinbase… so… they are just starting their own prediction markets as well… 
Within just the last, year no less than 12 major organisations including CME Group, Sports Illustrated and Trump Media’s Truth Social have launched or co-hosted their own predictions markets, so that no matter what platform you happen to be using, you can conveniently punt your rent money on whether aliens will be confirmed before GTA 6 is released. 
Like a lot of modern financial developments, it would almost be funny if it wasn’t going to have such devastating consequences on average people. 
But hopefully by now, you already knew all of this… what most people HAVEN’T noticed so far though, is the businesses that stand to make the most money out of all of this… and spoiler alert… it’s not the market facilitators themselves…

snippet.title: Where Science Moves Progress Follows
snippet.description:
Global scientific mobility drives innovation—what happens when migration is restricted by war, politics, or policy?

Ina Ganguli, professor of economics at @UMassEconomics & Director of @umass_cssi, shares her research on the global mobility of scientists and its critical role in innovation. From Nobel Prize–winning breakthroughs to startup leadership, she shows how high-skilled immigration fuels the knowledge economy. Ganguli reflects on the historical brain drain from the former Soviet Union, the global impact of the vaccines developed by immigrant scientists, and how conflicts—like the war in Ukraine—can derail scientific ecosystems. She warns that barriers to migration and collaboration risk undermining the next generation of discovery and argues for policies that support scientific exchange, protect displaced researchers, and invest in international collaboration.

Learn more about her work: https://websites.umass.edu/iganguli/

#healthcare #jobs #money 

----
I know it’s not going to come as a shock to any of you watching when I say that the Healthcare industry in America is incredibly broken… 
We spend almost double most other advanced economies, and yet we have measurably worse outcomes, lower life expectancy, higher infant mortality, more easily preventable deaths, far lower early intervention methods not to mention the general stress that goes along with a trip to the hospital which means a lot of people just… don’t go until it’s too late… 
Now again, I know none of this is shocking to you anymore (even though it really should be), but these frictions, failures and financial incentives have all become so ingrained into a system that has in turn become so ingrained into our country that it raises a rather concerning question… 
Would it even be possible to fix the healthcare system… without destroying the economy in the process? 
The USA is the largest market in the world thanks to the disproportionate share of our economy dedicated to consumer spending… 
This is a statistic that even I have highlighted here before on this channel because it makes us look like we just love buying overpriced trucks and useless consumer junk, and while maybe that’s still true, if you remove healthcare spending from this equation we are actually right in line with most other peer countries… 
Put another way, if we actually demolished the healthcare system and built something somewhat efficient in its place, we would cut out as much as 10% of our GDP… 
Now 10% of our entire economic output going towards spinning the wheels of medical bureaucracy isn’t great… but this broken window still represents millions of jobs not to mention… a lot of our financial system… they might contribute nothing outside of justifying their own existence, but now that they are there, getting rid of them without a backup plan is going to be deeply damaging. 
Now I know what you might be thinking, just because something is hard, doesn’t mean we shouldn’t do it, and even for the people who don’t believe in socialised medicine the bureaucratic bloat in healthcare is still a problem… but it’s also important to realise that no policy maker wants to preside over millions of lost jobs, even if it would fix one of the biggest ongoing burdens on the nation… 
Oh yeah and one last thing, before all of you non Americans start feeling too smug about the rock and a hard place we have wedged ourselves into, it’s probably worth exploring how we have exported this issue across the world to the point where there is a pretty good chance we are making YOUR health outcomes worse as well…

snippet.title: The Invisible Economy | TRAILER
snippet.description:
As data, intellectual property, and intangible assets eclipse physical capital, how do we ensure that policy, society, and institutions keep pace?

In this series, renowned economist Rohinton Medhora guides us through the fundamental shifts redefining value, labor, governance, and global cooperation in the 21st century. The Invisible Economy offers an essential roadmap for navigating the world we’re already living in—and the one that’s rapidly unfolding.

Learn more at http://invisibleeconomy.org

Directed by Matthew Kulvicki
Produced by Nick Alpha

snippet.title: Grant Cardone: Bitcoin Has None of Real Estate’s Problems
snippet.description:
Real estate investors are dealing with insurance, tenants, evictions, taxes, repairs, and liquidity problems. Grant Cardone says Bitcoin has none of those problems.

In this Commercial Observer interview, Brian Pascus asks Grant Cardone about his real estate and Bitcoin strategy, how Cardone Capital is thinking about cryptocurrency, tokenization, investor liquidity, and artificial intelligence. Grant breaks down why he believes Bitcoin can act as a long-term upside layer on top of real estate, why he still protects the downside with cash flow and hard assets, and how tokenization could create liquidity for investors in traditionally illiquid real estate deals.

This is a direct look at how Grant Cardone is thinking about the next phase of commercial real estate, Bitcoin, AI, and investor access.

In this video, you’ll learn how to:

Compare the problems of real estate with the advantages of Bitcoin
Understand why Grant sees Bitcoin as a potential long-term upside asset
Protect downside risk with real estate, cash flow, tax write-offs, and appreciation
Use tokenization as a potential liquidity tool for real estate investors
Think about AI as an assistant without losing focus on the main business

snippet.title: The Case for a New Bretton Woods
snippet.description:
How do we prepare for a world of constant shocks—climate disasters, financial crises, pandemics, conflict, and inequality?

Kevin Gallagher, Director of @globaldevelopmentpolicycenter, calls for a new international financial architecture to meet the demands of the 21st century. Drawing on insights from his book "The Case for a New Bretton Woods", Gallagher outlines five foundational principles for a system that is more resilient, inclusive, and fit for the polycrisis era.

From rising interest rates to mounting climate emergencies, our current institutions are falling short. But change is possible—and necessary.

Learn more about his work:
https://www.bu.edu/gdp/profile/kevin-p-gallagher/

About the book:
https://www.bu.edu/gdp/2022/01/18/the-case-for-a-new-bretton-woods/

▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬

ABOUT JASMINE DILUCCI, JD, CPA, EA

Jasmine DiLucci has specialized in tax since high school when she first became licensed to represent taxpayers before the IRS.

Now as a tax attorney and CPA, she works with individuals and business owners across the nation to on Tax Planning, CFO Advisory, and IRS Tax Resolution

How Jasmine Got Here…

18: Became an Enrolled Agent, licensed to represent taxpayers before the IRS.
22: Earned an Accounting Degree and a Master’s in Finance.
23: Became a CPA 
24: Stepped into leadership as she took over her own CPA firm
26-28: Juggled full-time studies at SMU Law while she was growing her CPA firm.
28: Graduated from law school 4th in her class and became an Attorney, all while managing her CPA firm.
29-31: Expanded her CPA firm to seven figures, with a focus on delivering top-notch service and exceptional value to every client.
32: Launched Tax Leverage to offer free online education and combat the rise of “tax gurus,” aiming to provide real, accessible tax knowledge.
Today: She’s dedicated to running her firm and leveraging her expertise to educate and empower others, helping individuals and businesses navigate the complexities of taxes and finance.

▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬

Disclaimer:  This information on this channel is for educational purposes only and does not constitute professional legal or tax advice.
